title: Generation isolation keeps staged effects invisible until publication and falsifies read-your-own-writes as one-generation refinement
semanticClaim: Analysis for one Gamma generation observes exactly the reaction-start state M_t.
A staged synthesis candidate does not replace semantic current/admitted input before publication.
After publication, the resulting M_(t+1) may be analyzed by the next Gamma generation.
For an A->B->C witness, one isolated generation stops at B while read-your-own-writes reaches C, so the cascade is observably not one-generation refinement.
explicitPremises: GPR-01 single-transformer decomposition is the selected semantic model for one Gamma generation.
Pre-publication semantic current remains the reaction-start state.
Publication is the boundary that exposes the complete successor to a later generation.
exclusions: No concrete CPU/WASM/WebGPU memory-fence implementation is proved here.
No partition/schedule invariance is claimed here; that is GPR-04.
No prohibition exists on B becoming input to a later Gamma after publication.
The finite A/B/C witness is external proof machinery only.
